in-protoreaster-nodosus.title: Chocolate Chip Sea Star
in-protoreaster-nodosus.summary: A sea star named for its dark "chocolate chip" knobs. Hardy for a sea star but not reef safe.
rows: About 1' 3 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 30 cm (11.8 in) across (SeaLifeBase)
No. Adults eat soft corals, sponges, tubeworms and clams
Carnivore. Meaty foods; adults also eat sessile invertebrates
Indo-West Pacific: from Seychelles to Australia and Japan
notes: Needs high water quality and does not tolerate high nitrate.
Wants a large tank with a mature sand bed several inches deep; keep away from triggers and puffers.
